title: Runway Weave: Quarterly sprint blueprint for Hosted API + Model Cohorts
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary:
Runway Weave is a quarterly planning artifact and execution blueprint focused on aligning Hosted API product priorities with model-catalog curation and capacity hedging. The goal is to produce a prioritized sprint pack (3–4 sprints) that: 1) surfaces the model cohorts we commit to for the quarter, 2) defines canary and blitz rollout windows, 3) allocates Dedicated capacity hedges and autoscaling guardrails, and 4) ties OKRs/metrics to concrete acceptance criteria and eval sets.

Background and motivation:
As model churn and usage patterns accelerate, teams need a predictable way to map product OKRs to the operational work that keeps Hosted API SLAs stable while enabling model rotations. Past quarters showed gaps between catalog health signals (quality regressions), capacity planning, and rollout sequencing — causing last-minute rollbacks or degraded latencies. This blueprint introduces a repeatable cadence for selecting cohorts, sequencing canaries, and pre-authorizing capacity buffers.

Scope (what this ticket owns):
- Finalize cohort definitions (Tier A/B/C) and selection criteria for the quarter.
- Define canary windows and rollback thresholds for Hosted API model swaps.
- Reserve Dedicated capacity hedges per cohort and document autoscaling policy triggers.
- Produce a concrete sprint backlog with owners, estimates, and gating evals.
- Surface required Console dashboards and alerts for rollout observability.

Out of scope:
- Low-level kernel tuning or runtime kernel shipping (handled in ENG tickets).
- Long-term model training or model architecture work not tied to rollout readiness.

Why now:
- Upcoming Q2 demand forecast and a scheduled major model rotation in March require coordinated planning.
- Need to reduce rollback incidents by 50% and keep 95th percentile tail latency within SLO during canaries.

Deliverables:
- Sprint blueprint document with sprint-by-sprint checklist and owners.
- Canary playbook (steps, metrics, thresholds).
- Capacity hedging table (GPU pool reservations, burst lanes, cost estimate).
- Dashboards and alert runbook entries scoped for Console release catalog-2026.03.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort definitions (A/B/C) published and approved by PM+Research+Eng
Canary playbook with concrete thresholds (error rate, 95/99 latency, quality eval delta) validated in staging
Capacity hedge booked for Tier A cohort with cost estimate and burn rate projection
Sprint backlog created and triaged into Cycle 2026-W05 with owners and estimates
Pre-deployment dashboard panels (per-model token cost, per-route latency, canary health) created in Console and linked

risks_mitigation: Risk: Model quality regression during canary. Mitigation: require pass on curated eval set and automatic rollback at quality delta > 2%.
Risk: Insufficient Dedicated capacity during high demand. Mitigation: pre-book hedge lanes and enable burst autoscaling with throttled quotas for non-critical tenants.
Risk: Console observability gaps. Mitigation: ship baseline dashboard before canary and run a tabletop exercise with on-call and SRE.
Risk: Cross-team misalignment on rollouts. Mitigation: weekly cross-functional review and a final 'go/no-go' 48 hours before canary start.
